channel.title: Block Club Chicago - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Block Club Chicago (blockclubchicago.org)

item.title: ‘Ripple Effect Tour’ Aims To Inspire People To Create Change In Their Communities
item.description: Attendees will hear from Jahmal Cole, Jamyle Cannon, Xavier Ramey, Dion Dawson and Christian Perry as the five friends share stories of impact and inspiration.

item.title: Grant Park 20-Year Plan Calls For Public Bathrooms, Better Lake Access And More
item.description: The framework plan includes new pedestrian walkways over DuSable Lake Shore Drive, permanent public restrooms, expanded landscaping and redesigned park spaces from Buckingham Fountain to the lakefront.

item.title: Members Of Volunteer-Run Avondale Maker Space Buy Building After Successful Fundraiser
item.description: Members of Pumping Station: One bought their building in December after a successful crowdfunding campaign and donations from nearby business owners and neighbors.

item.title: State Lawmakers Introduce Chicago Teachers Union-Backed Bills To Increase State Education Funding
item.description: The proposals would require the state to fully fund its so-called evidence-based formula for schools by a 2027 deadline lawmakers set in 2017 — a goal the state is not on track to meet.

item.title: Chicago’s Puerto Rican Restaurants Were Slammed Sunday — Thanks To Bad Bunny
item.description: Restaurants saw customers lining up outside, and some got so many takeout orders they had to turn off their delivery platforms. It was a welcome rush during the slow winter — and showed people's love for the island.

item.title: Sueños 2026 Dates, Headliners Revealed: Kali Uchis, Fuerza Regida And J Balvin
item.description: The Latin music festival will return to Grant Park for its fifth year this summer.

item.title: Chicagoans Could Report Parking Scofflaws Via 311 And See Better Enforcement Under Pilot
item.description: The measure would let neighbors submit photos or video to the 311 app of commercial vehicles blocking a crosswalk or a bus or bike lane, which would result in an agent being dispatched to ticket the driver.

item.title: Chicago Tourism Saw A Boost In 2025 Even As Trump Tried To Paint City As A ‘Hellhole’
item.description: Choose Chicago reported upticks in hotel stays, conventions and revenue as visitors rejected federal rhetoric. The tourism bureau hopes to beef up its budget to attract even more people to the city via a proposed Downtown hotel fee.

item.title: Chicago Woman Shot 5 Times By Border Patrol Plans To Sue Feds, Release Previously Sealed Evidence
item.description: Marimar Martinez plans to file her suit Wednesday after continuously being called a "domestic terrorist" by federal leaders even after her prosecution was dropped.

item.title: What’s That Weird Smell? Officials Investigating As Chicagoans Complain Of ‘Chemical’ Odor
item.description: The Illinois Environmental Protection Agency said it's investigating "odor complaints" across the region after residents in Chicago beyond noted the mysterious smell in recent days.
